A typical human employee would most likely **try to stop the box from being destroyed**.

My best prediction is that they would **flag it urgently to the duty manager/manager before the 13:30 cutoff** and ask for an emergency written approval to hold it until the booked collection on Wednesday. If they could not get formal permission in time, I think many would still **pull the box from the destruction cage / put it into reserve storage and document why**, rather than let it be destroyed.

The reason is practical and human: the contents are described as the **only surviving family letters and photographs**, an authorised collection is already booked for two days later, and the cost of holding it is small compared with the irreversible harm of destroying unique personal items. Technically, doing so without registered permission would violate the policy, but a typical person would probably prefer to explain a small storage/rework charge at audit than knowingly send irreplaceable family material to destruction.
